sanskrit: te rāvaṇavadhaṃ dṛṣṭvā devagandharvadānavāḥ jagmus tais tair vimānaiḥ svaiḥ kathayantaḥ śubhāḥ kathāḥ
english: Having witnessed the slaying of Rāvaṇa, the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas departed in their various celestial vehicles, relating auspicious tales to one another.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya vadhaṃ ghoraṃ rāghavasya parākramam suyuddhaṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca sugrīvasya ca mantritam
english: They narrated the terrible slaying of Rāvaṇa, the valor of Rāghava, the glorious battle of the monkeys, and the counsel of Sugrīva—

sanskrit: anurāgaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca saumitrer lakṣmaṇasya ca kathayanto mahābhāgā jagmur hṛṣṭā yathāgatam
english: —and the devotion and heroism of Saumitri Lakṣmaṇa; thus those greatly blessed ones departed rejoicing by the same way they had come.

sanskrit: rāghavas tu rathaṃ divyam indradattaṃ śikhiprabham anujñāya mahābhāgo mātaliṃ pratyapūjayat
english: Rāghava, that greatly blessed one, then dismissed the divine chariot given by Indra — radiant as a flame — and duly honored Mātali.

sanskrit: rāghaveṇābhyanujñāto mātaliḥ śakrasārathiḥ divyaṃ taṃ ratham āsthāya divam evāruroha saḥ
english: Granted leave by Rāghava, Mātali — charioteer of Śakra — mounted that divine chariot and ascended directly to heaven.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu divam ārūḍhe surasārathisattame rāghavaḥ paramaprītaḥ sugrīvaṃ pariṣasvaje
english: When that best of the gods' charioteers had ascended to heaven, Rāghava, filled with supreme joy, embraced Sugrīva.

sanskrit: pariṣvajya ca sugrīvaṃ lakṣmaṇenābhivāditaḥ pūjyamāno hariśreṣṭhair ājagāma balālayam
english: Having embraced Sugrīva, saluted by Lakṣmaṇa, and honored by the foremost of the monkeys, he came to the army's encampment.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā rāmaḥ samīpaparivartinam saumitriṃ sattvasaṃpannaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dīptatejasaṃ
english: Then Rāma spoke to Saumitri Lakṣmaṇa — endowed with great virtue and blazing with splendor — who stood close by his side:

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇam imaṃ saumya laṅkāyām abhiṣecaya anuraktaṃ ca bhaktaṃ ca mama caivopakāriṇam
english: "O gentle one, consecrate Vibhīṣaṇa here as king of Laṅkā — he who is devoted to me, loyal to me, and has rendered me great service."

sanskrit: eṣa me paramaḥ kāmo yad imaṃ rāvaṇānujam laṅkāyāṃ saumya paśyeyam abhiṣiktaṃ vibhīṣaṇam
english: "This is my deepest wish, O gentle one: to see this younger brother of Rāvaṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, consecrated as ruler of Laṅkā."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu saumitrī rāghaveṇa mahātmanā tathety uktvā tu saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sauvarṇaṃ ghaṭam ādade
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Rāghava, Saumitri replied "So be it" with great joy and took up a golden vessel.

sanskrit: ghaṭena tena saumitrir abhyaṣiñcad vibhīṣaṇam laṅkāyāṃ rakṣasāṃ madhye rājānaṃ rāmaśāsanāt
english: With that vessel Saumitri consecrated Vibhīṣaṇa as king amid the rākṣasas of Laṅkā, acting on Rāma's command.

sanskrit: abhyaṣiñcat sa dharmātmā śuddhātmānaṃ vibhīṣaṇam tasyāmātyā jahṛṣire bhaktā ye cāsya rākṣasāḥ
english: That righteous-souled one consecrated the pure-souled Vibhīṣaṇa, and his ministers and the rākṣasas devoted to him rejoiced greatly.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvābhiṣiktaṃ laṅkāyāṃ rākṣasendraṃ vibhīṣaṇam rāghavaḥ paramāṃ prītiṃ jagāma sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Seeing Vibhīṣaṇa consecrated as lord of the rākṣasas in Laṅkā, Rāghava together with Lakṣmaṇa was filled with supreme delight.

sanskrit: sa tad rājyaṃ mahat prāpya rāmadattaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ prakṛtīḥ sāntvayitvā ca tato rāmam upāgamat
english: Having obtained that great kingship bestowed by Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa pacified his subjects and then came before Rāma.

sanskrit: akṣatān modakāṃl lājān divyāḥ sumanasas tathā ājahrur atha saṃhṛṣṭāḥ paurās tasmai niśācarāḥ
english: Then the joyous night-roaming citizens brought him unbroken grains, sweetmeats, parched rice, divine flowers, and garlands.

sanskrit: sa tān gṛhītvā durdharṣo rāghavāya nyavedayat maṅgalyaṃ maṅgalaṃ sarvaṃ lakṣmaṇāya ca vīryavān
english: The invincible and valiant Vibhīṣaṇa accepted those auspicious and propitious offerings and presented them all to Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: kṛtakāryaṃ samṛddhārthaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmo vibhīṣaṇam pratijagrāha tat sarvaṃ tasyaiva priyakāmyayā
english: Seeing Vibhīṣaṇa's purpose accomplished and his aim fulfilled, Rāma accepted all of it solely out of desire to please him.

sanskrit: tataḥ śailopamaṃ vīraṃ prāñjaliṃ pārśvataḥ sthitam abravīd rāghavo vākyaṃ hanūmantaṃ plavaṃgamam
english: Then Rāghava addressed the monkey Hanūmant — that hero who resembles a mountain, standing at his side with palms joined in reverence:

sanskrit: anumānya mahārājam imaṃ saumya vibhīṣaṇam praviśya rāvaṇagṛhaṃ vinayenopasṛtya ca
english: "O gentle one, with the permission of this great king Vibhīṣaṇa, enter the abode of Rāvaṇa and, approaching with humility—"

sanskrit: vaidehyā māṃ kuśalinaṃ sasugrīvaṃ salakṣmaṇam ācakṣva jayatāṃ śreṣṭha rāvaṇaṃ ca mayā hatam
english: "—tell Vaidehī that I am well, together with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa, O foremost among the victorious, and that Rāvaṇa has been slain by me."

sanskrit: priyam etad udāhṛtya maithilyās tvaṃ harīśvara pratigṛhya ca saṃdeśam upāvartitum arhasi
english: "Having delivered this joyful news to the Maithilī, O lord of the monkeys, and having received her message in return, you should come back."

sanskrit: iti pratisamādiṣṭo hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ praviveśa purīṃ laṅkāṃ pūjyamāno niśācaraiḥ
english: Thus commissioned, Hanūmān — son of the wind-god — entered the city of Laṅkā, honored by the night-roaming rākṣasas along the way.

sanskrit: praviśya tu mahātejā rāvaṇasya niveśanam dadarśa śaśinā hīnāṃ sātaṅkām iva rohiṇīm
english: Entering the dwelling of Rāvaṇa, that one of great splendor saw Sītā bereft of her moon, like Rohiṇī separated from the moon and filled with terror.

sanskrit: nibhṛtaḥ praṇataḥ prahvaḥ so 'bhigamyābhivādya ca rāmasya vacanaṃ sarvam ākhyātum upacakrame
english: Approaching her quietly, bowing low and stooping respectfully, he saluted her and began to relate in full the message of Rāma.

sanskrit: vaidehi kuśalī rāmaḥ sasugrīvaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ kuśalaṃ cāha siddhārtho hataśatrur ariṃdamaḥ
english: "O Vaidehī, Rāma is well, together with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa; the subduer of foes, his purpose accomplished and his enemy slain, sends you his greetings."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇasahāyena rāmeṇa haribhiḥ saha nihato rāvaṇo devi lakṣmaṇasya nayena ca
english: "O goddess, Rāvaṇa has been slain by Rāma aided by Vibhīṣaṇa, together with the monkeys, and by the wise strategy of Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṃ rāmo vīras tvāṃ raghunandanaḥ abravīt paramaprītaḥ kṛtārthenāntarātmanā
english: "The heroic Rāma, the delight of the Raghu line, having inquired after your welfare, spoke with supreme joy in his heart, his purpose fulfilled:"

sanskrit: priyam ākhyāmi te devi tvāṃ tu bhūyaḥ sabhājaye diṣṭyā jīvasi dharmajñe jayena mama saṃyuge
english: "'I bring you joyful tidings, O goddess, and I honor you all the more: by good fortune you live, O one who knows righteousness, through my victory in battle.'"

sanskrit: labdho no vijayaḥ sīte svasthā bhava gatavyathā rāvaṇaḥ sa hataḥ śatrur laṅkā ceyaṃ vaśe sthitā
english: "'Victory has been won by us, O Sītā — be at ease, let your anguish pass. That enemy Rāvaṇa is slain, and this Laṅkā has been brought under control.'"

sanskrit: mayā hy alabdhanidreṇa dhṛtena tava nirjaye pratijñaiṣā vinistīrṇā baddhvā setuṃ mahodadhau
english: "'This vow made by me — who went without sleep and remained steadfast in winning your liberation — has been fully fulfilled by building a bridge across the great ocean.'"

sanskrit: saṃbhramaś ca na kartavyo vartantyā rāvaṇālaye vibhīṣaṇavidheyaṃ hi laṅkaiśvaryam idaṃ kṛtam
english: "'You who dwell in the abode of Rāvaṇa need have no anxiety, for this sovereignty of Laṅkā has been placed under the authority of Vibhīṣaṇa.'"

sanskrit: tad āśvasihi viśvastā svagṛhe parivartase ayaṃ cābhyeti saṃhṛṣṭas tvaddarśanasamutsukaḥ
english: "'Therefore be at ease, confident that you are now in your own home; and this one comes joyfully, eager for the sight of you.'"

sanskrit: evam uktā samutpatya sītā śaśinibhānanā praharṣeṇāvaruddhā sā vyājahāra na kiṃ cana
english: Thus addressed, Sītā — whose face resembles the moon — leapt up, but overcome with surging joy she spoke not a single word.

sanskrit: abravīc ca hariśreṣṭhaḥ sītām apratijalpatīm kiṃ tvaṃ cintayase devi kiṃ ca māṃ nābhibhāṣase
english: The foremost of monkeys said to Sītā, who remained silent and unresponsive: "Why do you ponder, O goddess? Why do you not speak to me?"

sanskrit: evam uktā hanumatā sītā dharme vyavasthitā abravīt paramaprītā harṣagadgadayā girā
english: Thus addressed by Hanūmān, Sītā — steadfast in righteousness — spoke with supreme joy, her voice choked and trembling with delight:

sanskrit: priyam etad upaśrutya bhartur vijayasaṃśritam praharṣavaśam āpannā nirvākyāsmi kṣaṇāntaram
english: "Having heard this joyful news concerning my lord's victory, I was overcome with a rush of delight and rendered speechless for a moment."

sanskrit: na hi paśyāmi sadṛśaṃ cintayantī plavaṃgama matpriyākhyānakasyeha tava pratyabhinandanam
english: "For I cannot find, however much I ponder, O monkey, a fitting reward here to offer you in return for having conveyed this joyful tidings of mine."

sanskrit: na ca paśyāmi tat saumya pṛthivyām api vānara sadṛśaṃ matpriyākhyāne tava dātuṃ bhavet samam
english: "Nor do I see, O gentle monkey, anything on this entire earth that could be given to you as equal recompense for conveying this joyful news to me."

sanskrit: hiraṇyaṃ vā suvarṇaṃ vā ratnāni vividhāni ca rājyaṃ vā triṣu lokeṣu naitad arhati bhāṣitum
english: "Silver or gold, or gems of many kinds, or sovereignty over the three worlds — none of these is worthy even to speak of in this regard."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu vaidehyā pratyuvāca plavaṃgamaḥ pragṛhītāñjalir vākyaṃ sītāyāḥ pramukhe sthitaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Vaidehī, the monkey replied, standing before Sītā with his palms joined together in reverence:

sanskrit: bhartuḥ priyahite yukte bhartur vijayakāṅkṣiṇi snigdham evaṃvidhaṃ vākyaṃ tvam evārhasi bhāṣitum
english: "You alone are worthy to speak such words of tender affection — you who are devoted to your lord's welfare and happiness, and who desire your lord's victory."

sanskrit: tavaitad vacanaṃ saumye sāravat snigdham eva ca ratnaughād vividhāc cāpi devarājyād viśiṣyate
english: "Your words, O gentle one, are full of substance and tender feeling; they surpass a multitude of gems of every kind, and even sovereignty over the realm of the gods."

sanskrit: arthataś ca mayā prāptā devarājyādayo guṇāḥ hataśatruṃ vijayinaṃ rāmaṃ paśyāmi yat sthitam
english: "And in substance I have already obtained the goods of sovereignty over the gods and more, in that I behold Rāma victorious and his enemy slain — this is my reward."

sanskrit: imās tu khalu rākṣasyo yadi tvam anumanyase hantum icchāmy ahaṃ sarvā yābhis tvaṃ tarjitā purā
english: "But if you grant permission, I wish to kill all these rākṣasī women who formerly threatened and terrorized you—"

sanskrit: kliśyantīṃ patidevāṃ tvām aśokavanikāṃ gatām ghorarūpasamācārāḥ krūrāḥ krūratarekṣaṇāḥ
english: "—those of dreadful appearance and behavior, cruel and with even crueler eyes, who tormented you — who hold your husband as your deity — when you were in the Aśoka grove."

sanskrit: rākṣasyo dāruṇakathā varam etaṃ prayaccha me icchāmi vividhair ghātair hantum etāḥ sudāruṇāḥ
english: "Those rākṣasīs of terrible speech — grant me this boon: I wish to slay these utterly dreadful ones by various means of destruction."

sanskrit: muṣṭibhiḥ pāṇibhiś caiva caraṇaiś caiva śobhane ghorair jānuprahāraiś ca daśanānāṃ ca pātanaiḥ
english: "With fists, with hands, and with feet, O beautiful one, with terrible blows of the knee, and by knocking out their teeth—"

sanskrit: bhakṣaṇaiḥ karṇanāsānāṃ keśānāṃ luñcanais tathā bhṛśaṃ śuṣkamukhībhiś ca dāruṇair laṅghanair hataiḥ
english: "—by biting off their ears and noses, by tearing out their hair, and by striking those dried-mouthed ones with terrible blows and leaping upon them—"

sanskrit: evaṃprakārair bahubhir viprakārair yaśasvini hantum icchāmy ahaṃ devi tavemāḥ kṛtakilbiṣāḥ
english: "—by many such acts of punishment, O renowned goddess, I wish to kill these ones who have done you wrong, O mistress."

sanskrit: evam uktā mahumatā vaidehī janakātmajā uvāca dharmasahitaṃ hanūmantaṃ yaśasvinī
english: Thus addressed by the great-minded one, the renowned Vaidehī — daughter of Janaka — spoke to Hanūmān in words consonant with righteousness:

sanskrit: rājasaṃśrayavaśyānāṃ kurvatīnāṃ parājñayā vidheyānāṃ ca dāsīnāṃ kaḥ kupyed vānarottama
english: "Who would be angry at slave-women who are subject to royal authority, who act by another's command, and who must comply with orders? O foremost of monkeys—"

sanskrit: bhāgyavaiṣamyayogena purā duścaritena ca mayaitat prāpyate sarvaṃ svakṛtaṃ hy upabhujyate
english: "All this has come upon me through the working of adverse fate and through past misdeeds; for one experiences the fruits of one's own actions."

sanskrit: prāptavyaṃ tu daśāyogān mayaitad iti niścitam dāsīnāṃ rāvaṇasyāhaṃ marṣayāmīha durbalā
english: "I am certain that I had to suffer this through the conjunction of circumstance. I, being helpless, endure the conduct of Rāvaṇa's slave-women."

sanskrit: ājñaptā rāvaṇenaitā rākṣasyo mām atarjayan hate tasmin na kuryur hi tarjanaṃ vānarottama
english: "These rākṣasīs threatened me under Rāvaṇa's orders; now that he is slain, O foremost of monkeys, they would not threaten me anymore."

sanskrit: ayaṃ vyāghrasamīpe tu purāṇo dharmasaṃhitaḥ ṛkṣeṇa gītaḥ śloko me taṃ nibodha plavaṃgama
english: "There is an ancient verse in keeping with righteousness, sung by a bear in the presence of a tiger — hear it from me, O monkey:"

sanskrit: na paraḥ pāpam ādatte pareṣāṃ pāpakarmaṇām samayo rakṣitavyas tu santaś cāritrabhūṣaṇāḥ
english: "'Another does not incur the sin belonging to those who perform sinful acts; the noble, who are adorned by righteous conduct, must observe the proper code of behavior.'"

sanskrit: pāpānāṃ vā śubhānāṃ vā vadhārhāṇāṃ plavaṃgama kāryaṃ kāruṇyam āryeṇa na kaś cin nāparādhyati
english: "Whether toward the wicked or the virtuous, even those deserving of death, O monkey, a noble one must show compassion — for there is no one who never transgresses."

sanskrit: lokahiṃsāvihārāṇāṃ rakṣasāṃ kāmarūpiṇam kurvatām api pāpāni naiva kāryam aśobhanam
english: "Even toward rākṣasas who roam the worlds delighting in harm and who take whatever form they wish, even while committing sins, nothing unworthy should be done."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu hanumān sītayā vākyakovidaḥ pratyuvāca tataḥ sītāṃ rāmapatnīṃ yaśasvinīm
english: Thus addressed by Sītā, Hanūmān — skilled in speech — replied to Sītā, the renowned wife of Rāma:

sanskrit: yuktā rāmasya bhavatī dharmapatnī yaśasvinī pratisaṃdiśa māṃ devi gamiṣye yatra rāghavaḥ
english: "You are truly the righteous and renowned wife of Rāma, befitting him. Give me your message to carry back, O goddess — I shall go to where Rāghava is."

sanskrit: evam uktā hanumatā vaidehī janakātmajā abravīd draṣṭum icchāmi bhartāraṃ vānarottama
english: Thus addressed by Hanūmān, Vaidehī — daughter of Janaka — said: "I desire to see my husband, O foremost of monkeys."

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā hanumān pavanātmajaḥ harṣayan maithilīṃ vākyam uvācedaṃ mahādyutiḥ
english: Hearing those words of hers, Hanūmān — son of the wind-god, of great radiance — spoke these words, filling the Maithilī with joy:

sanskrit: pūrṇacandrānanaṃ rāmaṃ drakṣyasy ārye salakṣmaṇam sthiramitraṃ hatāmitraṃ śacīva tridaśeśvaram
english: "You shall see Rāma, O noble lady — his face like the full moon — together with Lakṣmaṇa, firm in friendship and his enemy destroyed, as Śacī sees the lord of the thirty gods."

sanskrit: tām evam uktvā rājantīṃ sītāṃ sākṣād iva śriyam ājagāma mahāvego hanūmān yatra rāghavaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to Sītā — who shone like Śrī herself made manifest — the swift Hanūmān came to where Rāghava was.

sanskrit: sa uvāca mahāprajñam abhigamya plavaṃgamaḥ rāmaṃ vacanam arthajño varaṃ sarvadhanuṣmatām
english: The monkey, skilled in meaning, approached Rāma — most wise and best among all bowmen — and spoke these words to him:

sanskrit: yannimitto 'yam ārambhaḥ karmaṇāṃ ca phalodayaḥ tāṃ devīṃ śokasaṃtaptāṃ maithilīṃ draṣṭum arhasi
english: "She on whose account this entire undertaking began and its fruits have ripened — that goddess Maithilī, scorched by sorrow, you should now behold."

sanskrit: sā hi śokasamāviṣṭā bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇā maithilī vijayaṃ śrutvā tava harṣam upāgamat
english: "For she — the Maithilī — though overwhelmed with grief and her eyes clouded with tears, upon hearing of your victory, was filled with joy."

sanskrit: pūrvakāt pratyayāc cāham ukto viśvastayā tayā bhartāraṃ draṣṭum icchāmi kṛtārthaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam
english: "And she, trusting in our earlier bond of confidence, said to me: 'I desire to see my husband, his purpose accomplished, together with Lakṣmaṇa.'"

sanskrit: evam ukto hanumatā rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ agacchat sahasā dhyānam āsīd bāṣpapariplutaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Hanūmān, Rāma — best among upholders of righteousness — suddenly fell into deep contemplation, his eyes flooded with tears.

sanskrit: dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niśvasya medinīm avalokayan uvāca meghasaṃkāśaṃ vibhīṣaṇam upasthitam
english: Sighing long and deeply, his gaze cast down to the earth, he spoke to Vibhīṣaṇa — who resembles a cloud — standing at hand:

sanskrit: divyāṅgarāgāṃ vaidehīṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitām iha sītāṃ śiraḥsnātām upasthāpaya māciram
english: "Have Vaidehī anointed with divine fragrant pastes, adorned with divine ornaments, and bathed with her hair washed, and bring Sītā here without delay."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa tvaramāṇo vibhīṣaṇaḥ praviśyāntaḥpuraṃ sītāṃ strībhiḥ svābhir acodayat
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, the eager Vibhīṣaṇa entered the inner apartments and urged Sītā through his own women attendants:

sanskrit: divyāṅgarāgā vaidehī divyābharaṇabhūṣitā yānam āroha bhadraṃ te bhartā tvāṃ draṣṭum icchati
english: "O Vaidehī, anointed with divine fragrant pastes and adorned with divine ornaments, mount the palanquin — may it be auspicious for you; your husband desires to see you."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu vaidehī pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇam asnātā draṣṭum icchāmi bhartāraṃ rākṣasādhipa
english: Thus addressed, Vaidehī replied to Vibhīṣaṇa: "O lord of the rākṣasas, I wish to see my husband without bathing first."

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ yathāha rāmo bhartā te tat tathā kartum arhasi
english: Hearing those words of hers, Vibhīṣaṇa replied: "As your husband Rāma has said, so it is fitting that you act."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā maithilī bhartṛdevatā bhartṛbhaktivratā sādhvī tatheti pratyabhāṣata
english: Hearing those words of his, the Maithilī — who holds her husband as her deity, who has taken the vow of devotion to her husband, that virtuous one — replied "So be it."

sanskrit: tataḥ sītāṃ śiraḥsnātāṃ yuvatībhir alaṃkṛtām mahārhābharaṇopetāṃ mahārhāmbaradhāriṇīm
english: Then Sītā, her hair bathed, adorned by young women, wearing precious ornaments and clothed in costly garments—

sanskrit: āropya śibikāṃ dīptāṃ parārdhyāmbarasaṃvṛtām rakṣobhir bahubhir guptām ājahāra vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: —was placed upon a blazing-bright palanquin covered with the most precious cloth and guarded by many rākṣasas, and Vibhīṣaṇa brought her forward.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya mahātmānaṃ jñātvābhidhyānam āsthitam praṇataś ca prahṛṣṭaś ca prāptāṃ sītāṃ nyavedayat
english: Approaching the great-souled Rāma and perceiving that he was absorbed in deep thought, Vibhīṣaṇa bowed humbly and joyfully announced that Sītā had arrived.

sanskrit: tām āgatām upaśrutya rakṣogṛhaciroṣitām harṣo dainyaṃ ca roṣaś ca trayaṃ rāghavam āviśat
english: Upon hearing of her arrival — she who had long dwelt in the house of the rākṣasas — three emotions simultaneously seized Rāghava: joy, dejection, and anger.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārśvagataṃ dṛṣṭvā savimarśaṃ vicārayan vibhīṣaṇam idaṃ vākyam ahṛṣṭo rāghavo 'bravīt
english: Then, seeing Vibhīṣaṇa standing at his side and deliberating with grave reflection, the joyless Rāghava spoke these words:

sanskrit: rākṣasādhipate saumya nityaṃ madvijaye rata vaidehī saṃnikarṣaṃ me śīghraṃ samupagacchatu
english: "O gentle lord of rākṣasas, ever devoted to my victory — let Vaidehī come swiftly into my presence."

sanskrit: sa tad vacanam ājñāya rāghavasya vibhīṣaṇaḥ tūrṇam utsāraṇe yatnaṃ kārayām āsa sarvataḥ
english: Understanding that command of Rāghava, Vibhīṣaṇa quickly set about clearing the way on all sides.

sanskrit: kañcukoṣṇīṣiṇas tatra vetrajharjharapāṇayaḥ utsārayantaḥ puruṣāḥ samantāt paricakramuḥ
english: Men wearing armor-coats and turbans, bearing rattling cane staffs, moved about on all sides clearing and dispersing the crowd.

sanskrit: ṛkṣāṇāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca rākṣasānāṃ ca sarvataḥ vṛndāny utsāryamāṇāni dūram utsasṛjus tataḥ
english: The crowds of bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas being driven back on all sides were dispersed far away from there.

sanskrit: teṣām utsāryamāṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dhvanir utthitaḥ vāyunodvartamānasya sāgarasyeva nisvanaḥ
english: From all of them as they were being dispersed arose a roar like the sound of the ocean being churned up by the wind.

sanskrit: utsāryamāṇāṃs tān dṛṣṭvā samantāj jātasaṃbhramān dākṣiṇyāt tadamarṣāc ca vārayām āsa rāghavaḥ
english: Seeing them being driven away on all sides in a commotion, Rāghava — out of both courtesy and impatience — ordered them to stop.

sanskrit: saṃrabdhaś cābravīd rāmaś cakṣuṣā pradahann iva vibhīṣaṇaṃ mahāprājñaṃ sopālambham idaṃ vacaḥ
english: And Rāma, agitated, his eyes burning as if with fire, spoke these reproachful words to the greatly wise Vibhīṣaṇa:

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ mām anādṛtya kṛśyate 'yaṃ tvayā janaḥ nivartayainam udyogaṃ jano 'yaṃ svajano mama
english: "Why, disregarding me, are these people being harassed by you? Stop this effort — these people are my own people."

sanskrit: na gṛhāṇi na vastrāṇi na prākārās tiraskriyāḥ nedṛśā rājasatkārā vṛttam āvaraṇaṃ striyaḥ
english: "Not houses, not garments, not walls are screens of concealment — the proper veil of a woman is her conduct; such is not the way a woman is honored by a king."

sanskrit: vyasaneṣu na kṛcchreṣu na yuddhe na svayaṃvare na kratau no vivāhe ca darśanaṃ duṣyate striyaḥ
english: "In times of misfortune, in hardship, in battle, at a svayaṃvara, at a sacrifice, or at a wedding — the sight of a woman is not a fault."

sanskrit: saiṣā yuddhagatā caiva kṛcchre mahati ca sthitā darśane 'syā na doṣaḥ syān matsamīpe viśeṣataḥ
english: "This Sītā has been through war and has stood in great hardship; there is no fault in seeing her, especially in my presence."

sanskrit: tad ānaya samīpaṃ me śīghram enāṃ vibhīṣaṇa sītā paśyatu mām eṣā suhṛdgaṇavṛtaṃ sthitam
english: "Therefore bring her swiftly into my presence, O Vibhīṣaṇa — let Sītā see me standing here surrounded by the company of friends."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa savimarśo vibhīṣaṇaḥ rāmasyopānayat sītāṃ saṃnikarṣaṃ vinītavat
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, the reflective Vibhīṣaṇa humbly and respectfully led Sītā into Rāma's presence.

sanskrit: tato lakṣmaṇasugrīvau hanūmāṃś ca plavaṃgamaḥ niśamya vākyaṃ rāmasya babhūvur vyathitā bhṛśam
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva, and the monkey Hanūmān, having heard Rāma's words, became greatly distressed.

sanskrit: kalatranirapekṣaiś ca iṅgitair asya dāruṇaiḥ aprītam iva sītāyāṃ tarkayanti sma rāghavam
english: From his harsh manner and gestures showing indifference toward his wife, they surmised that Rāghava seemed displeased with Sītā.

sanskrit: lajjayā tv avalīyantī sveṣu gātreṣu maithilī vibhīṣaṇenānugatā bhartāraṃ sābhyavartata
english: The Maithilī, shrinking with shame into her own limbs, accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa, moved toward her husband.

sanskrit: sā vastrasaṃruddhamukhī lajjayā janasaṃsadi rurodāsādya bhartāram āryaputreti bhāṣiṇī
english: She, her face half-concealed in her garment, wept with shame in that assembly of people as she drew near to her husband, speaking the words "O noble son."

sanskrit: vismayāc ca praharṣāc ca snehāc ca paridevatā udaikṣata mukhaṃ bhartuḥ saumyaṃ saumyatarānanā
english: With wonder, with surging joy, with love, and with lament she gazed up at her husband's gentle face — she whose own face was yet more gentle.

sanskrit: atha samapanudan manaḥklamaṃ sā suciram adṛṣṭam udīkṣya vai priyasya vadanam uditapūrṇacandrakāntaṃ vimalaśaśāṅkanibhānanā tadāsīt
english: Then, gazing long upon the beloved face of her husband — radiant as the risen full moon in its beauty — she whose own face resembled the pure moon put aside the weariness of her heart, and thus she stood.
